name: Elixir
note: development began in 2011; rewritten lineage released in 2012; 1.0 released in 2014
typeSystem: Dynamic and strong, built on Erlang's type model, with a gradual set-theoretic type system under active development. Elixir 1.18 added partial inference and checking; Elixir 1.20 extended gradual inference and checking across all language constructs without requiring annotations.
runtime: Compiles to BEAM bytecode, the same virtual machine used by Erlang, giving full interoperability with the Erlang/OTP ecosystem.

runtimes.name: BEAM VM
runtimes.role: The same Erlang virtual machine, giving Elixir the same massive-concurrency, fault-tolerant runtime as Erlang.

runtimes.name: BEAM JIT (OTP 24+)
runtimes.role: Translates BEAM instructions to native code as modules are loaded.

compilers.name: elixirc
compilers.role: Compiles Elixir source to BEAM bytecode (.beam files).

concurrencyModel: Inherited from Erlang/OTP: lightweight processes ordinarily interact through asynchronous message passing and are supervised in fault-tolerant OTP trees. BEAM also provides explicitly shared runtime services such as ETS.

codeExample.caption: Hello, World! plus a recursive factorial
codeExample.source:
defmodule Hello do
  def fact(0), do: 1
  def fact(n), do: n * fact(n - 1)
end

IO.puts(Hello.fact(10))
